subject: Biology
title: Probiotics and Prebiotics
description: A quick, practical guide to Probiotics and Prebiotics.

hook.text: Probiotics are live microbes you consume to benefit your gut. Prebiotics feed the ones already there.

buildup.text: Yogurt, kimchi, and sauerkraut contain live bacteria cultures that may support gut health.

discovery.text: Prebiotics are fibers like inulin that pass through your stomach and feed beneficial gut bacteria.

twist.text: Most probiotic supplements lack strong clinical evidence. The strains and doses matter enormously.

climax.text: Fecal transplants—transferring a healthy microbiome—have cured severe gut infections.

punchline.text: Feed your microbes well. They'll feed you back.

quiz.question: What is the difference between probiotics and prebiotics?
options: Probiotics are live microbes; prebiotics feed them
Prebiotics are live microbes; probiotics feed them

details.summary: Probiotics are live beneficial microorganisms taken to improve gut health, while prebiotics are dietary fibers that feed beneficial gut bacteria. Together they aim to maintain a healthy microbiome balance, though scientific evidence for their benefits varies widely by strain and condition.
details.whyItMatters: The probiotics market exceeds $50 billion but many products lack solid evidence. Understanding what probiotics can and cannot do helps consumers make informed choices and encourages better clinical research into microbiome interventions.
takeaways: Evidence supports specific probiotic strains for antibiotic-associated diarrhea
Prebiotics like inulin and resistant starch feed beneficial gut bacteria
Most commercial probiotic claims are not supported by rigorous clinical trials

faq.question: Do probiotic supplements actually work?
faq.answer: Some specific strains have good evidence for specific conditions like antibiotic-associated diarrhea and irritable bowel syndrome. However, most commercial products lack strain-specific evidence. Not all probiotics survive stomach acid to reach the intestines.

faq.question: What is the difference between probiotics and prebiotics?
faq.answer: Probiotics are live microorganisms you ingest. Prebiotics are non-digestible food ingredients, mainly fibers, that selectively feed beneficial gut bacteria already living in your colon. Eating prebiotic foods like garlic, onions, and whole grains supports your existing microbiome.
